pharmacology.text: Synthetic cannabinoids (also known as synthetic marijuana, noids, herbal incense, K2, or spice) are a class of compounds that bind to cannabinoid receptors to produce cannabis-like subjective effects. Like THC, most synthetic cannabinoids bind to the same cannabinoid receptors in the brain and are often sold as legal alternatives.

uses.text: Like THC, most synthetic cannabinoids bind to the same cannabinoid receptors in the brain and are often sold as legal alternatives. Synthetic cannabinoids are usually sprayed or soaked into dry herbs to look more like marijuana, but pure powder is also available for sale on online research chemical markets.

sideEffects.en: They are often far stronger than cannabis and switch the CB1 receptor fully on. They can cause a racing heart, chest pain, vomiting, severe anxiety, psychosis, seizures, kidney injury and strokes, and some have caused deaths. Regular use can lead to dependence with a difficult withdrawal.
sideEffects.zh: 它們往往比大麻強得多，會完全活化CB1受體。它們可能造成心跳加速、胸痛、嘔吐、嚴重焦慮、精神病、癲癇發作、腎臟損傷與中風，部分已造成死亡。經常使用可能導致依賴，並伴隨難熬的戒斷症狀。
sideEffects.zhHans: 它们往往比大麻强得多，会完全活化CB1受体。它们可能造成心跳加速、胸痛、呕吐、严重焦虑、精神病、癫痫发作、肾脏损伤与中风，部分已造成死亡。经常使用可能导致依赖，并伴随难熬的戒断症状。

fact.en: Many of the first synthetic cannabinoids sold as Spice were research compounds made by the chemist John W. Huffman at Clemson University, which is why so many carry the initials JWH.
fact.zh: 最早以Spice之名販售的合成大麻素中，有許多是克萊姆森大學化學家約翰．哈夫曼所製造的研究用化合物，這也是為什麼這麼多種合成大麻素帶有JWH的縮寫。
fact.zhHans: 最早以Spice之名贩售的合成大麻素中，有许多是克莱姆森大学化学家约翰．哈夫曼所制造的研究用化合物，这也是为什么这么多种合成大麻素带有JWH的缩写。
